title: Chana Masala
subtitle: North Indian spiced chickpea curry
excerpt: Chickpeas cooked in a deeply spiced, tangy tomato and onion sauce with cumin, coriander, amchur, and garam masala. The most satisfying vegetarian curry in the North Indian repertoire: hearty, complex, and better the day after it is made.

recipe.sourceNotes: Chana masala (chickpea curry) is eaten across North India and Pakistan, where it is known as chole in Punjab. It is the dish most closely associated with the Punjabi dhaba (roadside restaurant) and is eaten for breakfast with bhature (fried bread) or puri in the classic combination of chole bhature. The dish is distinguished from other chickpea curries by the use of dried mango powder (amchur), which adds a distinctive sour note, and by the dark colour from black cardamom, cloves, and long frying of the onion and spice paste. Using dried chickpeas soaked overnight is the standard; tinned chickpeas produce an acceptable but less textured result.

content.text: Fry the onion until very deep golden, almost caramelised; this is the base flavour. Add the ground spices and cook them in the fat for a full minute before adding the tomatoes. The chickpeas need at least 20 minutes of simmering in the sauce to absorb the flavours; a shorter simmer produces a flat-tasting result.

items.preparation: dried; soaked overnight and boiled until tender; or 2 x 400g tins, drained
or amchur (dried mango powder) if available

content.text: Heat the oil in a large pan over medium heat. Cook the onion for 15 minutes until deep golden and beginning to caramelise. Add the garlic, ginger, and all the ground spices. Cook for 1 to 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Add the tinned tomatoes. Cook over medium heat for 8 to 10 minutes until the sauce is thick and the oil separates at the edges. Add the cooked or tinned chickpeas with 200 ml of water. Season.

Simmer for 20 to 25 minutes until the sauce is thick and has been absorbed into the chickpeas. Add the vinegar or amchur for sourness. Taste and adjust. Serve with basmati rice or pitta bread, scattered with fresh coriander.
